enonce_markdown: Which type of synovial joint is found at the hip?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Synovial joints are classified by the shape of the bone ends and the movements they allow. A rounded head fitting into a cup allows movement in many directions.

### Solution

At the hip, the rounded head of the femur fits into the cup-shaped socket of the pelvis. This is a ball-and-socket joint. A hinge joint (knee, elbow) moves in one plane, a pivot joint (neck) rotates, and a gliding joint (wrist) slides.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Hinge joint
Ball-and-socket joint
Pivot joint
Gliding joint

enonce_markdown: What is the main function of synovial fluid in a movable joint?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Each part of a joint has its own job: some parts join, some cushion and some lubricate.

### Solution

Synovial fluid is secreted by the synovial membrane and fills the joint cavity. It acts as an oil and so lubricates the joint, reducing friction between the bone ends. Joining bone to bone is the job of ligaments, and joining muscle to bone is the job of tendons.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: It joins the muscle to the bone
It joins one bone to another bone
It lubricates the joint to reduce friction
It makes red blood cells for the body

enonce_markdown: Fon swims the crawl stroke, moving his whole arm in large circles at the shoulder. Which statement explains why the shoulder can do this?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The range of movement of a joint depends on its type. Match the movement described to the joint shape that allows it.

### Solution

Movement in all directions, including rotation, is possible only at a ball-and-socket joint. The rounded head of the humerus fits in the shallow socket of the scapula. A hinge joint allows movement in one plane only and a gliding joint only allows small sliding movements.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: It is a ball-and-socket joint, which allows movement in all directions
It is a hinge joint, which allows movement in one plane only
It is a pivot joint, which allows only rotation about an axis
It is a gliding joint, which allows bones to slide over each other

enonce_markdown: Which row correctly pairs a type of synovial joint with an example found in the human body?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Learn each joint type with one reliable example: hinge (one plane), ball-and-socket (all directions), pivot (rotation), gliding (sliding).

### Solution

The joints in the fingers allow bending and straightening in one plane, so they are hinge joints. The knee is a hinge, not a pivot joint. The hip is ball-and-socket, not gliding. The elbow is a hinge, not ball-and-socket.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Pivot joint: knee
Gliding joint: hip
Ball-and-socket joint: elbow
Hinge joint: finger

enonce_markdown: A synovial joint is surrounded by a capsule and its bone ends are covered with a smooth layer. Describe how the following help the joint to work: (i) cartilage, (ii) ligaments, (iii) synovial fluid. *(3 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For each structure state what it is made of or where it lies, then say what it does for the joint.

### Solution

(i) **Cartilage** is a smooth, slightly flexible layer covering the ends of the bones. It reduces friction and absorbs shock.

(ii) **Ligaments** are tough, slightly elastic bands joining bone to bone across the joint. They hold the bones in position and prevent dislocation.

(iii) **Synovial fluid** fills the joint cavity. It lubricates the joint and so lets the bone ends move easily with little wear.

enonce_markdown: After an accident, the cartilage at a man's hip joint is worn away and most of the synovial fluid has leaked out. Which statement best explains why movement at this joint is now painful?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Link each damaged structure to the job it normally does, then predict what happens when that job is no longer done.

### Solution

Cartilage normally cushions the bone ends and synovial fluid lubricates them. Without both, the bone ends rub directly against each other with nothing to cushion or lubricate them, causing friction and pain. Ligaments and tendons are not mentioned as damaged, so the bones are still held and moved. Bone marrow is inside the bones and is not affected.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The muscles can no longer be attached to the bones because the tendons have been destroyed
The ligaments can no longer join the bones, so the two bones move apart
The bone marrow can no longer make blood cells, so the joint receives too little oxygen
The bone ends now rub directly on each other because nothing cushions or lubricates them
